items.question: What is natural numeric sorting?
items.answer: Standard alphabetical sorting places "10" before "2". Natural sorting treats embedded numbers as quantities so that 2 comes before 10.

items.question: Is the sorting algorithm stable?
items.answer: Yes. When items compare equal (for instance, case-insensitive duplicates like "Apple" and "apple"), their original relative order is strictly preserved.

items.question: How does duplicate removal handle letter casing?
items.answer: When duplicate removal is enabled with case-insensitivity, the tool keeps the very first occurrence found in the list and removes subsequent variants.

items.question: Can I sort a list of full names by last name?
items.answer: Yes. Enabling "Sort by Last Word" extracts the trailing word of each entry (such as the surname) to collate names alphabetically.

items.question: What input delimiters can I use?
items.answer: You can split items by line breaks, commas, semicolons, whitespace, tabs, or a custom delimiter string.

items.question: Does the sorter handle accented letters and non-English alphabets?
items.answer: Yes. Collation is powered by Intl.Collator which respects international language collation rules, correctly grouping accented and non-Latin characters.

items.question: Is sorting idempotent?
items.answer: Yes. Sorting an already sorted list produces the identical list without alterations, verified by automated fast-check property testing.

items.question: Can I reverse the sort order?
items.answer: Yes. You can switch between Ascending (A to Z, lowest to highest) and Descending (Z to A, highest to lowest) with a single click.
